html:
The Xixime were an Indigenous people of the Sierra Madre Occidental, in the mountains of today's Durango and Sinaloa in northwest Mexico. They lived in fortified villages in deep canyons, farmed maize and were feared by their neighbours, including the Acaxee, for warfare. Spanish reports, which may exaggerate, describe them as cannibals.

The Spanish of the Viceroyalty of New Spain came to their mountains for silver in the late 1500s. In 1610 the Xixime rose against them. Francisco de Urdiñola led an army that crushed the rising, executed its leaders and moved survivors into mission villages run by the Jesuits. Their missionary Hernando de Santarén was killed in the great Tepehuán Revolt of 1616 led by their neighbours the Tepehuane. Epidemics then destroyed the Xixime as a people.
